questions.question: Which statement best defines preterm labor?
choices: Labor with cervical change before 37 weeks
Any back pain during pregnancy
Rupture of membranes after term only
Every painless uterine tightening
questions.explanation: Preterm labor involves uterine contractions associated with cervical change before 37 weeks. Symptoms require obstetric assessment because history alone cannot confirm cervical change.

questions.question: A patient at 30 weeks reports pelvic pressure, low backache, and frequent tightening. What is the safest plan?
choices: Wait for the next monthly prenatal visit
Diagnose Braxton Hicks by telephone
Recommend strenuous activity to test whether symptoms resolve
Arrange prompt labor-and-delivery assessment
questions.explanation: This symptom cluster can represent preterm labor. Prompt obstetric evaluation preserves opportunities for diagnosis and gestational-age-specific intervention.

questions.question: Why is a routine digital cervical examination avoided when membrane rupture is possible?
choices: It prevents fluid leakage
It replaces sterile speculum assessment
It can increase ascending infection risk and shorten latency
It always confirms fetal lung maturity
questions.explanation: Digital examination can introduce organisms and is generally avoided until the obstetric team determines it is necessary, especially with possible preterm membrane rupture.

questions.question: Which presentation raises concern for intraamniotic infection after membrane rupture?
choices: A healed skin abrasion
Fever, uterine tenderness, foul fluid, and maternal or fetal tachycardia
Stable clear discharge without fever or pain
Isolated mild heartburn
questions.explanation: Fever, uterine tenderness, foul fluid, and tachycardia are concerning for infection and require urgent hospital obstetric management.

questions.question: Why can placental abruption be present even when visible bleeding is limited?
choices: Hemorrhage may be concealed behind the placenta
Abruption never causes bleeding
Blood pressure always rises before pain
Fetal status cannot be affected
questions.explanation: Abruption can produce concealed hemorrhage, uterine pain or tenderness, frequent contractions, and fetal compromise despite limited external blood loss.

questions.question: A patient says fetal movement is much lower than their usual pattern. What is the best response?
choices: Reassure because some movement was felt yesterday
Wait until the next scheduled visit
Use an office Doppler alone to rule out fetal compromise
Direct prompt obstetric assessment rather than relying on one universal kick number
questions.explanation: A meaningful decrease from the patient's established movement pattern is an urgent warning sign. A single heart-tone check does not replace appropriate fetal assessment.

questions.question: What is the best first interpretation of persistent clear fluid leakage at 33 weeks?
choices: A condition that can wait several days
Proof of active labor without examination
Possible preterm prelabor rupture of membranes requiring obstetric evaluation
Normal urine leakage until proven otherwise at home
questions.explanation: Persistent leakage may represent PPROM. Timely evaluation is needed to assess membrane status, infection, labor, gestational age, and fetal condition.

questions.question: Why does gestational age need to be established early in obstetric triage?
choices: It replaces maternal vital signs
It changes neonatal risk, treatment opportunities, transfer needs, and delivery planning
It is relevant only after birth
It determines whether bleeding is visible
questions.explanation: Management of preterm symptoms depends heavily on gestational age, including potential corticosteroids, neuroprotection, neonatal capability, and delivery decisions.

questions.question: Which action best reflects the FNP boundary in possible preterm birth?
choices: Recognize urgency and transfer to obstetric care for protocol-based cervical, fetal, and treatment decisions
Prescribe all tocolytics by telephone
Perform repeated digital examinations in a general clinic
Delay referral until fetal fibronectin is available
questions.explanation: The FNP identifies the risk and correct setting. Specialized testing and interventions depend on obstetric protocols, contraindications, membrane status, and fetal assessment.

questions.question: What makes an obstetric triage referral closed-loop?
choices: Telling the patient to go somewhere without a destination
Placing a referral for next month
Assuming another clinician received the message
Documenting the destination, handoff, transport plan, arrival or result, and follow-up ownership
questions.explanation: Closed-loop triage confirms where the patient is going, how they will arrive, that the receiving team understands the concern, and who follows results.
